													738 text Step 1
													739 heading Identify Known Values, Value: 2
														740 text Identify Known Values
													741 text Start by writing down what information you have, such as frequency, wavelength, or speed. For example, you might know the frequency is 5 Hz and the wavelength is 2 meters.

736 container 3 of 7
													737 text 3 of 7
													738 text Step 2
													739 heading Select the Right Formula, Value: 2
														740 text Select the Right Formula
													741 text Decide which version of the wave speed equation fits your problem. Use v = λf to find speed, or rearrange it to solve for wavelength or frequency.

736 container 4 of 7
													737 text 4 of 7
													738 text Step 3
													739 heading Substitute Values, Value: 2
														740 text Substitute Values
													741 text Plug your known numbers into the formula. For example, v = 2 m × 5 Hz.

736 container 5 of 7
													737 text 5 of 7
													738 text Step 4
													739 heading Calculate and Check Units, Value: 2
														740 text Calculate and Check Units
													741 text Do the math and make sure your answer has the correct units (like m/s for speed). Double-check that your units make sense.

736 container 6 of 7
													737 text 6 of 7
													738 text Step 5
													739 heading Interpret the Result, Value: 2
														740 text Interpret the Result
													741 text Think about what your answer means. Does the speed seem reasonable for the type of wave? Understanding the result helps you connect math to real-world situations.

742 container 2 of 7
													743 text 2 of 7
													744 text Step 1
													745 heading Calculate the Frequency, Value: 2
														746 text Calculate the Frequency
													747 image
													748 button Zoom image
													749 text Frequency is the number of vibrations completed each second.
													750 text f = number of vibrations / time
													751 text Substitute the known values:
													752 text f = 40.0 / 30.0 s
													753 text f = 1.33 Hz
													754 container
														755 text The oscillator produces approximately  1.33 waves each second .

742 container 3 of 7
													743 text 3 of 7
													744 text Step 2
													745 heading Calculate the Wave Speed, Value: 2
														746 text Calculate the Wave Speed
													747 image
													748 button Zoom image
													749 text Wave speed is the distance traveled divided by the travel time.
													750 text v = d / t
													751 text Substitute the known values:
													752 text v = 4.25 m / 10.0 s
													753 text v = 0.425 m/s
													754 container
														755 text The wave travels along the rope at  0.425 meters per second .

742 container 4 of 7
													743 text 4 of 7
													744 text Step 3
													745 heading Select the Wave Speed Equation, Value: 2
														746 text Select the Wave Speed Equation
													747 image
													748 button Zoom image
													749 text The wave speed equation connects wave speed, wavelength, and frequency.
													750 text v = λ f
													751 text Because the question asks for wavelength, rearrange the equation:
													752 text λ = v / f

742 container 5 of 7
													743 text 5 of 7
													744 text Step 4
													745 heading Substitute the Values, Value: 2
														746 text Substitute the Values
													747 image
													748 button Zoom image
													749 text Substitute the calculated wave speed and frequency:
													750 text λ = 0.425 m/s / 1.33 Hz
													751 text Remember that a hertz is equal to one vibration per second, so the seconds cancel and the answer is measured in meters.

													744 text Step 5

														746 text Calculate the Wavelength
													747 text λ = 0.319 m
													748 text The wavelength is:
													749 text λ = 0.319 m
													750 container
														751 text This means the distance between two consecutive wave crests is approximately  0.319 meters , or  31.9 centimeters .
